q: we introduce FrontierRefactor, a benchmark of 60 qualified engineering tasks spanning four scales
r: Include: new benchmark with repeated trials, speedup and cost metrics for coding agents on repository-level refactoring (evaluation method contribution).

q: Passing those tests can require information the description never states
r: Include: audit method for the validity of coding-agent benchmarks, applied to 35 published runs (contribution to evaluation method).

q: we introduce SWE-Clar, a benchmark grounded in real, high-value client commissions
r: Include: new benchmark of greenfield project-level development from natural-language requests, with acceptance tests and nine models compared.

q: We introduce SWE-Shift, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents
r: Include: new benchmark with matched Clean/Shifted controlled design over 17 coding-agent systems (evaluation method contribution).

q: three separate delegation studies with hidden behavioral checks
r: Include: experience report with multi-trial controlled studies of open-weight models as coding workers, with hidden checks and cost per verified success.

q: We introduce FeatureLoop, a benchmark of 61 human-reviewed tasks from 34 repositories
r: Include: new benchmark for feature-level development under evolving requirements, with new metrics and 12 models compared.

q: We developed a bootstrap prompt designed to set up both inputs from one round of human input
r: IC1: vision paper proposing an agent-swarm factory design (not yet evaluated); it is neither SDD, a context-file study nor an evaluation or comparison of coding agents.

q: we run a controlled study of iterative refactoring
r: Include: controlled study of Codex and Claude Code across five models with new behavioural signals and repeated turns (evaluation method).

q: We introduce FEATUREARC to evaluate coding agents on evolving features
r: Include: new benchmark for feature-level development with staged tasks, requirements and executable checks, plus an empirical study of agents.

q: we introduce CodeSpecWeave, a framework for synthesizing tasks with rich, interdependent specifications
r: EC5: main contribution is a task-synthesis and RL-training technique tested on existing benchmarks (DeepSWE, SWE-bench), with little added to evaluation method.
